what_happened: Task description's Remedy 1 assumes reviser-agent can SendMessage the live implement dispatch, but skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md Move 2 documents forwarding only agent (subagent_type) and model as Agent-tool arguments to dispatch[]/aux_dispatch[] rows -- no name: parameter is assigned, and SendMessage appears nowhere in agent-system/extensions/core except one unrelated hook (hooks/please-grant.sh). The literal notification mechanism needs either a Move 2 naming-convention addition (so reviser-agent can address the implement dispatch by a predictable name) or a file-sentinel alternative (mirroring the existing .blocker-research.json/.drift-inspection.json consumed-and-cleared idiom); recorded for the planning phase to resolve explicitly rather than assuming SendMessage works as literally described.

Verified the current byte-budget state directly rather than trusting the task description's framing: task #289 (which was to promote ORCHESTRATOR_BUDGET_GATE_MODE from warn to hard) has already landed -- scripts/verify-deploy.sh:207 now defaults to hard -- and skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md measures 21,476 B against its 21,500 B ceiling (24 B headroom), tighter than the description's 'becoming hard' framing implied. This sharpens the byte-budget constraint for the planning phase: essentially zero headroom remains for any SKILL.md prose addition.

Planning read of orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's cycle_plan_dispatch_hash() surfaced a STANDING OBLIGATION that invalidated the research report's Recommendation 2 (emit the plan's mtime at dispatch-build time): the implement agent checks off plan items every cycle, so an mtime/sha line in the implement dispatch block would have permanently rendered the IDENTICAL DISPATCH HALT inert unless orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (contended with 5 other tasks) were also edited. The plan was redesigned to emit only static content, which is also the better design since the correct freshness baseline is the agent's own first read, not dispatch-build time.
